hero.headline: Where the day ends slowly.
hero.subline: A boutique kasbah of fourteen rooms in the Agafay desert, an hour south of Marrakech.

story.headline_1: We built a small house in the desert,
story.headline_2: inside the longest hour of the day.
story.p1: Sunset Agafay is fourteen rooms wrapped around a courtyard of olive trees, an hour south of Marrakech and a world away from it. We bought the land in 2019 and spent four years rebuilding it stone by stone with masons from the valley. It opened, quietly, in the spring of 2025.
story.p2: There is a pool that catches the last of the sun, an old-world bar that opens at six, and dinners that begin when the muezzin sings. The rest is space, and the light. We hope you will stay long enough to notice it.

suites_section.title: Fourteen, no two alike.
suites_section.lede: Each room reworked from existing kasbah walls. Linen by Mtali, ceramics from Tameslouht.

rooms.name: Suite Agafay
rooms.brief: Built into the eastern wall and open to the full Agafay plateau. Raw tadelakt in desert ochre, a brass four-poster, and a soaking tub positioned to catch the morning light. The terrace faces due east — the first in the maison to see the sun.

rooms.name: Suite La Khoutoubia
rooms.brief: Named for the minaret just visible on clear mornings, this first-floor suite pairs an oversized bedroom with a private salon and a hammered-brass soaking tub. The salon doubles as a reading room and has its own west-facing window seat.

rooms.name: Suite Sunset
rooms.brief: Our signature corner room. Floor-to-ceiling shutters open directly onto the dunes, and a private plunge pool catches the full afternoon sun before the Atlas turns pink at dusk. The most requested room in the maison, for obvious reasons.

rooms.name: Family Suite
rooms.brief: Two connected rooms — each with its own bathroom — sharing a private courtyard and plunge pool. Designed for families or small groups who want complete privacy within the kasbah walls without feeling separated from the rest of the maison.

cinematic.quote: The desert here does not perform. It simply lasts longer than you do, and at six o'clock it lets the light go slowly enough that even hurried guests forget where they were going.

tables_section.title: Three rooms to eat & drink in.
tables_section.lede: Cooking from the valley, aperitifs at six, and one private table held twice a week.

tables.name: Le Souk
tables.lede: Long lunches under the pergola; dinners by candlelight when the muezzin sings.
tables.copy: Chef Yassine cooks entirely from what the valley and the coast provide. Slow-braised lamb on Tuesdays, seven-vegetable couscous every Friday, sea bream brought up from Essaouira on ice. The wine list is short and deliberately Moroccan-led — a few natural bottles, a house rosé, and one very good white Burgundy for those who insist.

tables.name: Bar Arish
tables.lede: An old-world bar that opens at six. Aperitifs, vermouths, and the longer cocktails after dark.
tables.copy: A brass counter, a back-bar of Moroccan bitters and aged vermouths, and a small terrace directly facing the dunes. The aperitif hour — six to seven-thirty — is the soul of the maison, and we keep it as unhurried as possible. After eight, the cocktails lengthen and the conversation follows suit.

tables.name: La Table d'Idriss
tables.lede: A fourteen-seat private table hosted by the founder.
tables.copy: Held on Wednesday and Saturday evenings on the upper terrace, around a single long farm table set for fourteen. The six-course menu is written each morning from whatever the Marrakech market provided. Idriss is present at every sitting. Reservations taken one week in advance; no printed menu, no separate wine list, very little ceremony.

experiences_section.title: Six small things to do here.
experiences_section.lede: A short list, kept short on purpose. We would rather do these well than offer twenty of them.

experiences.name: Sunrise on the Plateau
experiences.lede: An hour out across the hammada to watch the sun first reach the Atlas.

experiences.name: The Long Friday Lunch
experiences.lede: Couscous, mint tea, and three hours under the pergola — as it has always been done.

experiences.name: Hammam, Slow
experiences.lede: Black soap, rassoul, eucalyptus steam; ninety minutes ending with mint tea on the upper terrace.

experiences.name: Stargazing with Said
experiences.lede: Said brings out the small refractor; we bring out the brandy. Saturn most nights of the year.

experiences.name: Kasbah Drawing Lesson
experiences.lede: Sketch the courtyard with the Marrakech illustrator Lina Berrada. Paper and ink provided.

experiences.name: Aperitif on the Dunes
experiences.lede: We drive a low table out to the dunes; you bring the conversation. The bar stays open until the light is gone.

hammam_section.lede: The hammam is built into the lower walls of the kasbah, in tadelakt the colour of clay and rose. We keep the rituals traditional and the timing leisurely.

events_section.title: The kasbah, entirely yours.
events_section.lede: We host intimate gatherings of the kind that deserve a desert backdrop.

types.name: Wedding
types.lede: A kasbah wedding in a setting that requires no florist, no backdrop, no theme.
types.copy: We celebrate weddings for twelve or for eighty, managing every detail from the florals and lighting to the table plan and the last glass of champagne. The Agafay desert does the rest — no venue in Morocco has a more natural sense of occasion.

types.name: Private Gathering
types.lede: The kind of evening that has no programme and ends only when it should.
types.copy: Birthdays, anniversaries, intimate reunions, and milestone dinners. We set the long table, arrange the aperitif hour, order the flowers, and brief the kitchen. You choose the guest list and the hour; the desert provides everything else, including the light.

types.name: Corporate Retreat
types.lede: Exclusive use of the maison for the thinking that never happens in a conference room.
types.copy: Full buy-out of Sunset Agafay for leadership offsites, creative workshops, editorial shoots, and strategy sessions that require a change of scene. Complete F&B, private transfers from Marrakech-Menara, and a bespoke programme on request.

press_section.quote: One of those rare new openings that already feels as if it has always been there. The aperitif hour, especially, is a small masterpiece.

footer.bulletin_text: Four letters a year, written by the maison. No marketing.

experiences_page.hero_sub: A short list, kept short on purpose. Each experience is personally hosted and limited to a small number of guests.

events_page.hero_sub: We host intimate gatherings — weddings, private gatherings, and corporate retreats — for groups who understand that the setting matters.

transfers_page.hero_title: From the city to the desert.
transfers_page.hero_sub: Private, punctual, and arranged by the maison. Every transfer is handled personally — no third-party booking apps.

options.name: Airport Day Transfer
options.lede: A seamless morning or afternoon run from Marrakech-Menara to the kasbah gates.
options.copy: Our drivers meet you in arrivals with a name board. The route takes forty-five minutes on a clear day. Chilled water and wifi in the vehicle. Available 07:00 – 19:00.

options.name: Airport Night Transfer
options.lede: Late arrivals and early departures, handled quietly so the maison is never disturbed.
options.copy: For flights arriving or departing outside daylight hours. The same discreet service, with the added courtesy of a night-before confirmation. Available 19:00 – 07:00.

options.name: Private Transfer
options.lede: Bespoke road transfers to the medina, the coast, or wherever the day takes you.
options.copy: Use the vehicle for a half-day in the Marrakech souks, a trip to Essaouira, or an onward connection. Quoted individually by distance and hours. Minimum four-hour booking.

sunset_parties_page.hero_title: The hour when the desert performs.
sunset_parties_page.hero_sub: Three distinct formats, each built around the particular quality of Agafay light at dusk. A gathering, not an event.

parties.name: White Sunset Party
parties.lede: An all-white affair on the terrace as the sun drops behind the Atlas.
parties.copy: One request only: guests dress in white. The table is set in ivory linen and brass candleholders against the last hour of Agafay light. We open with an aperitif of Moroccan whites and cold mezze on the terrace; dinner is served by candlelight once the first stars appear. The evening runs 18:00 to midnight and is private hire only — no other guests on site.

parties.name: Pool Party
parties.lede: A long afternoon around the pool, with the Atlas as a permanent backdrop.
parties.copy: From noon until the sun disappears behind the dunes: shade cushions, cold Moroccan rosé, platters of mezze, and the particular quiet that a desert afternoon in forty degrees insists upon. Music from 16:00 — a resident DJ or live oud, your choice. The pool is reserved exclusively for your group. Runs noon to 20:00.

parties.name: Red Sunset Party
parties.lede: A curated cocktail gathering when the dunes turn deep ochre.
parties.copy: The most intimate of our three formats — held on the desert-facing terrace at the precise hour when the Agafay turns red. Pomegranate aperitifs, aged Moroccan reds, and warm mezze passed by hand. Strictly limited to twenty guests to preserve the atmosphere. Runs 18:30 to 22:00, all year round.
